observation.visible_scene: A close-up of a metal drafting compass standing on a white sheet of paper that already bears a faint, thin curved arc across the lower part of the frame. Two legs of the compass are visible, joined off the top of the frame; one leg's tip sits near the middle of the frame and the other leg extends toward an edge.
visible_changes: The compass rotates about the leg whose tip stays near the centre of the frame; the second leg swings from the right side of the frame, across the top, and reappears on the left side over the course of the clip.

As that swinging leg reaches the left side (around t=0.92s onward), its lower end resolves into a knurled metal holder with a dark point/lead tip that comes to rest near the left end of the faint arc.
The central leg's tip remains approximately fixed near the middle of the frame throughout, with only small positional shifts.
Several frames show pronounced motion blur on the moving leg, indicating continuous sweeping motion rather than a series of static poses.
The faint arc on the paper does not visibly grow, shrink, or change shape during the excerpt; it remains in roughly the same place relative to the frame.

The overall framing of the arc and the central leg stays largely constant, but the apparent thickness/visibility of the legs changes as the compass turns, consistent with a rotation of the instrument (with at most slight camera reframing).
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether an operator is holding the compass and in which direction the rotation started or will continue.
Whether the arc was drawn by this compass earlier or is pre-existing, and whether the dark tip is actively drawing or merely positioned.
The full structure of the compass hinge above the frame.
uncertain_details: It is not fully clear whether the apparent leftward sweep of the outer leg is pure compass rotation about a fixed pivot or partly a camera orbit; the stable position of the arc suggests the camera is mostly stationary.
The exact contact point of the swinging leg's tip on the paper, and whether the central tip is a needle pivot or a drawing point, is ambiguous due to blur and shallow focus.
